clue.text: Rule not enforced in the main ?

definitions.text: Rule not enforced in the main ?

parts.words: Rule not enforced in the main
parts.note: the main is the sea, so a rule that does not apply at sea is one that holds only ashore

explanation.surface: A regulation that is somehow ignored in the most important cases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The main' reads as 'mainly', but it is the old word for the open sea; the law that does not run at sea is the one that holds ashore.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means the established legal code of a country, which is land-based, unlike maritime law.

clue.text: Title given to James, novel

parts.note: Lord is a title of nobility
Jim is a familiar short form of the name James

explanation.surface: A man called James is honoured with a new title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like an adjective for the title but it is the definition: Joseph Conrad's novel of 1900.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Conrad wrote this book about a disgraced seaman, so it is a specific example of a novel.

clue.text: Powerful hymn-writer

definitions.meaning: units of electrical power, read cryptically as the measure of being powerful
Isaac ..., author of hymns such as 'O God, our help in ages past'

explanation.surface: A forceful composer of church songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Powerful' is stretched to mean 'units of power'; the surface treats it as praise of the hymn-writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Power is measured in units named after James Watt, and Isaac Watts was a leading English hymnist.

clue.text: Nazi holds Russian quarter for Prussian king

indicators.note: one name holding the others means they sit inside it

parts.note: Wilhelm Frick was a leading Nazi minister
Red was the common label for a Soviet Russian
E, east, is one of the four quarters of the compass

explanation.surface: A Nazi official detains a Russian soldier, all to do with a Prussian king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holds' puts the Russian and the quarter inside the Nazi's surname, just after its first letter; Frick was Hitler's Interior Minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Frederick the Great, Frederick William and others ruled Prussia, so the name is that of several of its monarchs.

clue.text: Park, made, we hear, for bird-watchers

indicators.note: says the word that follows is to be heard, not spelt

parts.note: a hide is a screened shelter from which people watch birds

explanation.surface: A park has been laid out, so they say, with bird-watchers in mind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made' is a link: a hide is something made for bird-watchers, and it sounds the same as the name of the London park.
explanation.definitionFit: Hyde Park is the large royal park in central London.

clue.text: Drink given for article in French newspaper

indicators.note: the article is set inside the paper's name

parts.note: Le Monde is the leading Paris daily
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone is offered a drink in return for writing a piece in a Paris paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Article' reads as a newspaper piece but it is the grammatical article A, put into LE MONDE after its N.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweet citrus soft drink, served cold.

clue.text: Old settler of lofty character

definitions.meaning: an old English gold coin, the kind of thing that settles a debt

explanation.surface: An early colonist with a high moral tone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settler' suggests a colonist; here it is something that settles a bill, a coin of medieval England.
explanation.definitionFit: The medieval gold coin worth a third of a pound was so called, and the adjective means honourable or high-minded.

clue.text: Earth's to be replaced by variable resistance

indicators.note: letters replaced are put back in new places, so the words before are rearranged

explanation.surface: An electrician warns that the earth wire must be swapped for a variable resistor.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like wiring instructions; 'to be replaced' hides the anagram signal 'be replaced' acting on EARTHS and TO.
explanation.definitionFit: This device is a resistor whose value can be adjusted to control current, used in dimmer switches.

clue.text: Gambles pay? That's about right

indicators.note: one word placed about another goes round it

parts.note: wages are pay for work

explanation.surface: A gambler asks whether betting pays, and is told that is about right.
explanation.definitionFit: Bets are stakes placed on an uncertain outcome, so gambles in the noun sense.

clue.text: Ramble on about not drinking the red sort of port

indicators.note: the first word goes round the pieces that follow it

parts.note: to roam is to wander or ramble
TT, teetotal, means abstaining from alcohol

indicators.note: a sort of red is a rearranged version of the word

explanation.surface: A wine bore goes on and on about the red served at a port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ramble on' looks like the definition of a talker, but 'on' is a link. 'Sort of' rearranges 'red' into ERD; 'port' reads as wine but is the Dutch harbour city.
explanation.definitionFit: This Dutch city is one of the largest harbours in Europe.

clue.text: He gets in a snake for tea!

indicators.note: the first piece gets into the second, so it sits inside it

parts.note: a boa is a large constricting snake

explanation.surface: A man climbs into a snake's coils in search of tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' looks like a man but is just its own two letters; the exclamation mark dresses the surface. Bohea was the old name for the best black China tea.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a black China tea, once the general name for the finest of them.

clue.text: A man of stone

definitions.meaning: an opaque, usually red, variety of quartz

explanation.surface: Someone describes a man of firm, stony character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of' links two definitions; the surface suggests a hard-hearted man.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a male first name, and also a red or brown quartz used as a semi-precious gem.

clue.text: Covering the case of The Five Orange Pips

definitions.meaning: a wrapper or casing, something that covers

definitions.text: the case of The Five Orange Pips
definitions.meaning: a Sherlock Holmes case in which the threat arrives as orange pips posted to the victims

explanation.surface: A summary of the Sherlock Holmes story of the five orange pips.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' reads as a detective's case, and it is one, but it also nods to a case as a cover. In Conan Doyle's story the pips arrive by post.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper wrapper covers a letter, and in the Holmes story the pips come inside one.

clue.text: Thanks to foreigners, a bit of old England

parts.note: merci is French for thank you

explanation.surface: Through help from overseas, a piece of old England was obtained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thanks to' reads as 'because of'; it is 'thanks, in a foreign tongue'.
explanation.definitionFit: It was an Anglo-Saxon kingdom of the English Midlands, a part of the country in early times.

clue.text: They might be looked down on by careless drivers

definitions.text: They might be looked down on by careless drivers

parts.words: They might be looked down on by careless drivers
parts.note: reads as things scorned by reckless motorists; literally, guides a driver glances down at instead of the road

explanation.surface: Things that bad drivers sneer at.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Looked down on' suggests scorn, but means literally glanced down at, as a careless motorist does at the guide on the lap.
explanation.definitionFit: Motorists consult these charts of routes, and reading one while at the wheel is careless.

clue.text: Trains the form-fillers

parts.note: reads like bureaucracy; the forms here are school classes, and those who fill them are pupils being taught

explanation.surface: Someone coaches the people who complete official paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Form' suggests paperwork; in a British school a form is a class, so its fillers are the pupils.
explanation.definitionFit: A school teaches its pupils, who fill its classes, called forms in Britain.

clue.text: Clue's not a tricky sort for our establishment abroad

indicators.note: a tricky sort of the words is a rearrangement of them

explanation.surface: This clue is not a difficult one to work out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tricky sort' reads as the clue's character, but it signals sorting CLUES NOT A into a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: The office of a country's official representative in a foreign city, so one of our national offices overseas.

clue.text: Percentage that's against the dance

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
the tango is a Latin American dance

explanation.surface: Someone resents paying a fee for the dance.
explanation.walkthrough: A Stock Exchange term: the percentage a buyer paid the seller for postponing settlement.
explanation.definitionFit: On the old London Stock Exchange this was a rate of interest paid for deferring a transaction, a percentage charge.

clue.text: Wood has not returned seafood

parts.note: a plank is a length of wood

indicators.note: a word returned is sent back, so it is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A diner complains that the timber is missing and the fish was not sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returned' turns NOT into TON. 'Seafood' is stretched: plankton are the food of sea creatures.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny drifting organisms in the ocean are the food of whales and fish, so literally food in the sea.

clue.text: Favourite sort of tie — small and dainty

parts.note: a pet is a favourite

indicators.note: a sort of tie is the word rearranged

explanation.surface: Describing a man's favourite kind of necktie as neat and slim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' turns TIE into ITE.
explanation.definitionFit: Used of a woman of slight, delicate build, from the French word for little.

clue.text: Bit of song to take quickly

definitions.meaning: a short fragment of a tune

explanation.surface: Grabbing a quick phrase of music.
explanation.definitionFit: It means a fragment of music overheard and also to grab something suddenly.

clue.text: Was perfect ?

parts.note: reads as 'used to be flawless'; in grammar, the perfect tense of 'was'

explanation.surface: Someone who was flawless once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perfect' is the grammar term: the perfect tense corresponding to 'was'. The other reading fits too: a former star who used to be perfect.
explanation.definitionFit: A faded celebrity is someone whose best days are past, and grammatically the phrase is the perfect of 'was'.

clue.text: Find mould at entering religious building

indicators.note: the word entering goes inside the building

parts.note: a temple is a place of worship

explanation.surface: A worshipper finds mould while going into a temple.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Find' is a link word. 'Mould' reads as fungus but means a pattern used to shape things.
explanation.definitionFit: A pattern or guide used to shape or cut identical pieces, as a mould is.

clue.text: Note written in vein of a scientist

indicators.note: the note is set inside the vein, as if written into it

parts.note: a lode is a vein of ore
G is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: A scientist's comment, set down in a characteristic manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vein' reads as 'manner' but is a seam of ore. Sir Oliver Lodge was a British physicist and radio pioneer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Oliver Lodge was a British physicist who worked on radio waves.

clue.text: Gets spirit to drink on return uproar results

parts.note: rum is a spirit

indicators.note: a word on return comes back, so it is read in reverse

parts.note: to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: Someone takes spirits to drink on getting back, and a row follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On return' turns SUP into PUS.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy disturbance or commotion, so an uproar.

clue.text: Really trying to take them

parts.note: the idiom 'take ...' means making a great effort, so these are what you take when trying hard

explanation.surface: Making a big effort to grab hold of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Them' points to the plural noun in the idiom; 'take' sounds like grabbing.
explanation.definitionFit: Great care and effort, as in the idiom about taking trouble over a job.

clue.text: Chilly sort of cake?

definitions.meaning: a cake with a sugar topping

explanation.surface: Asking whether a cake is a cold one.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means frozen or very cold, and also covered in sugar topping, as some cakes are.

clue.text: Summed up as Recorder did ?

definitions.meaning: had someone weighed up or understood, as in 'I've got him sized up'
what a tape machine did: recorded

explanation.surface: Describing how a court Recorder gave the summing-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recorder' reads as the judge of that title who sums up a trial; here it is a tape machine.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for having someone weighed up, and also recorded on magnetic tape.

clue.text: Fruit makes -heavenly Chinese drink perhaps

parts.note: the fruit's name contains the drink of the gods; the fruit is a smooth peach first grown in China

explanation.surface: A fruit that might give the Chinese a divine drink.
explanation.walkthrough: The name starts with the gods' drink, NECTAR, and China, the 'Celestial' (heavenly) Empire, is where the fruit first grew.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth-skinned variety of peach, its name built from the drink of the Greek gods.

clue.text: Shortest passage from the Bible ?

parts.note: a reading taking no time at all; split one word, it is the reading 'without a second'

explanation.surface: Asking which biblical passage is the briefest.
explanation.walkthrough: The church service has two readings; the later one's name split as 'second-less' says it lasts less than a second.
explanation.definitionFit: In Anglican services the later of the two Bible readings has this name.
